issues.description: Docstring typo 'stlib' should read 'stdlib' in the rendered deprecation directive.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged the same typo in the .. deprecated:: 4.3 block: 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`'. This renders into Sphinx output that users see when they hit the warning. Trivial one-character fix worth doing before merge.

issues.description: Deprecation warning message could be tightened to match the stdlib's separated design.
issues.detail: The runtime warning bundles redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr into one prescription and partly duplicates the docstring directive. Consider noting they are independent context managers and citing the deprecated-since version (4.3) for symmetry with the Sphinx directive.

issues.description: Deprecation test is loose: matches only the message tail and skips the stderr path.
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected's pytest.warns match anchors on the 'Please use...' suffix, so a prefix reword passes silently; match on something stable like 'deprecated' or the function name. A symmetric assertion exercising stderr=output would also round out coverage while the function still ships.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts this PR: a small, well-scoped deprecation of a bespoke context manager in favor of stdlib contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr, with internal callers migrated, a news fragment, and a warning test. No correctness, performance, or design concerns surfaced. Findings are all cosmetic: a 'stlib' typo in the rendered docstring, a slightly muddled warning message that could mirror the stdlib's separated primitives, and a loose test match. Fix the typo and ship.
